body: Monday, February 28 2022 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information available before 2022-02-28 00:00 UTC. Prices use completed prior sessions. Prepared retrospectively; later outcomes are excluded.

Macro Stance: Friday's violent relief rally has already been partly overtaken. The S&P 500 closed at 4,384.65 index points (+2.24% on the day, +0.10% over five sessions) and the Nasdaq 100 at 14,189.16 index points (+1.53%), while the VIX fell 2.73 points to 27.59 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Reuters framed it as investors digesting sanctions on Russia  [1] , after Fortune described the week's reversal as one of the incredible vaults in equity-market history  [2] . That rally priced the first sanctions package; The New York Times then reported the US and Europe will bar some Russian banks from SWIFT  [3] . Mixed: US earnings are less exposed than Europe's, but multiples rest on a Fed that experts quoted by Business Insider say will not rescue a meltdown  [4] .

Rates & Curve: The curve says the Fed matters more than the war. The 2Y closed at 1.55% and the 10Y at 1.97%, leaving 10Y-2Y at +42 bps, with the 3M at 0.33% and 10Y-3M at +164 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25). Over 20 observations the 2Y rose 37 bps from 1.18% and the 10Y 16 bps from 1.81%, so the spread compressed by 21 bps: the curve is positively sloped and the 20-observation move is a bear flattening, both up with the 2Y up more. Over five observations the 2Y added 6 bps and the 10Y was unchanged, meaning the safe-haven bid Reuters described on invasion day  [5]  only anchored the long end. Xinhua reported a Fed official signalling a March hike remains on track despite Ukraine  [6] .

New / Most Important: Two shifts matter. First, the SWIFT step, which CBC said Canada is joining  [7] , moves sanctions from named lenders to the payment rails, raising settlement risk for anyone still clearing Russian flows. Second, demand was already softening: The Conference Board said consumer confidence declined for a second consecutive month in February  [8] , and Builder reported pending home sales falling for a third straight month in January  [9] , against the largest annual consumer-price gain in 40 years  [10] . Corporate cash is going to buybacks, with CNBC reporting a record $27 billion Berkshire repurchase in 2021  [11] . The DXY slipped 0.54% to 96.62 index points on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25) after Reuters had reported the dollar near a two-year high on invasion day  [12] .

Playbook ✓: Action: hold US quality large caps and energy over long-duration growth, and keep index hedges on while the VIX sits at 27.59 index points. Trigger to add risk: the S&P 500 holding Friday's 4,384.65 close as markets absorb the SWIFT measures, with the VIX failing to regain 30.49, its late-January level (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). What changes the call: a front end that keeps rising while the 10Y stalls would deepen the bear flattening from +42 bps and signal tightening into a growth shock; Reuters has already reported louder calls for 50 bps rather than 25 bps in March  [13] . The State of the Union on March 1  [14]  tests whether Washington pairs sanctions with energy-price relief.

Macro Stance: Europe is where the weekend's escalation lands hardest. Friday's bounce lifted the STOXX 600 3.32% to 453.53 index points and the DAX 3.67% to 14,567.23 index points, yet both remain down 2.58% and 4.91% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Since then Europe has moved to remove Russian banks from SWIFT, per Global Finance  [15] , and to shut its airspace to Russian airlines while funding weapons purchases for Ukraine, per PBS  [16] . Bearish: the region carries the energy, banking and trade exposure that sanctions and counter-sanctions now target.

Activity & Inflation: The growth starting point was respectable, with Times of Malta reporting euro-zone growth jumping as virus restrictions eased  [17] . The price side is the problem: Eurostat put energy inflation at 27%  [18] , and The Guardian argued the war will fuel a sharp further hike  [19] . Dutch TTF gas closed at 94.42 EUR/MWh, down 29.70% on Friday but up 26.04% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), a volatility profile that makes industrial hedging expensive. ECB policymakers told Reuters not to go back on quicker taper plans  [20] , so the stagflation trade-off is live.

New / Most Important: Germany's U-turn is the regime change. DW reported a €100 billion commitment to defence spending  [21] , Reuters quoted Scholz calling it a response to 'Putin's war'  [22] , and Clean Energy Wire reported plans for strategic gas and coal reserves  [23] . Fiscal expansion for security and energy storage is inflationary at the margin, supportive for defence and grid suppliers, and a direct cost to taxpayers.

Playbook ✓: Action: underweight euro-area banks with Russian subsidiaries and energy-intensive cyclicals; overweight defence. Societe Generale closed at 28.45 EUR, down 12.09% over five sessions, while Rheinmetall closed at 107.05 EUR, up 11.00% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Trigger: add to the bank underweight if TTF rebuilds Friday's 29.70% drop. What changes the call: a credible negotiation track that takes TTF back below 92.30 EUR/MWh, its late-January level, which would ease the margin squeeze on industry and the inflation pressure on the ECB.

Macro Stance: China is trading as a policy-insulated onshore market and a sanctions-sensitive offshore one. The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,451.41 index points, up 0.63% on Friday and down only 1.13% over five sessions, while the Hang Seng closed at 22,767.18 index points, down 6.41% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Beijing's line, which PBS described as avoiding criticism of the Russian attack while calling for talks  [24] , keeps it outside the Western coalition; The New York Times reported US officials had repeatedly urged China to help avert the war  [25] . Mixed: onshore policy support is real, but the offshore market is pricing regulatory and geopolitical risk at the same time.

PMIs & Activity: The last private factory gauge was weak: Reuters reported January Caixin activity contracting as COVID lockdowns bit  [26] . Against that, China Daily reported industrial profits rebounding in 2021 as production improved  [27] , and Best Selling Cars Blog put January vehicle wholesales up 0.9% in a stable market  [28] . Structural drags show up regionally, with SCMP reporting a rust-belt province unveiling a population plan in the face of economic decline  [29] . Power investment is the bright spot: Global Times reported an expected record 75-90GW of solar additions  [30] . The next activity readings are the February surveys; until then the read is soft manufacturing and policy-led investment.

Credit Impulse: The policy direction is easier even before the credit numbers confirm it. Reuters reported that slowing inflation leaves room for policy easing  [31] , and Bloomberg described the People's Bank seizing the moment for stimulus as the Fed hikes  [32] . That divergence is the core of the China call: the US 2Y has risen 37 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25) while Beijing leans the other way. The constraint is transmission through a stressed property sector and a tighter grip on platform finance; The Japan Times reported regulators telling banks and state firms to report exposure to Jack Ma's Ant  [33] . Easing channelled through state lenders and infrastructure should lift onshore equities before it lifts household consumption.

Property: Property is still triage rather than recovery. Reuters reported Evergrande selling four projects to state-owned firms for $337 mln  [34] , and SCMP described Chinese firms picking away at its assets  [35] . CNBC reported Moody's downgrading Shimao as debt troubles drag on  [36] , and The Standard reported Fantasia being sued over its bond default  [37] . The pattern is a controlled transfer of viable projects into state hands, which limits systemic contagion but leaves private developers' offshore bondholders at the back of the queue. For equities, it means the property drag on steel, building materials and household wealth persists even as policy eases at the margin.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: The next policy signal is the annual 'two sessions', which SCMP previewed as Beijing plotting its course  [38] ; the growth target and fiscal quota will set the tone for the quarter. Hong Kong is already spending, with Al Jazeera reporting a $22bn budget as zero-COVID hammers businesses  [39] . Trade cuts both ways. Reuters reported Russia's trade flows shifting towards China as sanctions start  [40] , and Global Times quoted analysts saying the agricultural-trade impact on China is limited  [41] . Doubts over the phase-one deal, which SCMP asked was a 'historic failure'  [42] , and the Peterson Institute's finding that China bought none of the extra $200 billion of US exports  [43]  make secondary measures a tail risk if Beijing is seen to cushion Moscow.

Markets & Flows: Offshore internet is where the discount is applied. Tencent closed at 402.71 HKD, down 9.79% over five sessions, and Alibaba's Hong Kong line at 105.30 HKD, down 11.88%, while KWEB fell 9.04% and FXI 6.80% over the same span; ASHR, the onshore CSI 300 proxy, rose 0.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Reuters tied the rout to fresh fears of a regulatory crackdown  [44] , and Bloomberg reported Alibaba planning for a new normal of low growth  [45] . Primary-market appetite has faded too: Reuters reported Shein shelving its US IPO plan again on uncertain markets  [46] , and WSJ reported a US block-trading investigation hitting Morgan Stanley's plans to expand in China  [47] . The yuan is the counterpoint, with China Daily arguing it will remain an investor safe haven  [48] .

New / Most Important: The war has sharpened the Taiwan question for portfolios. Reuters reported Beijing insisting Taiwan is 'not Ukraine' as the island raised its alert level  [49] , and separately Taiwan warning of Chinese aircraft in its air defence zone  [50] . TSMC said it will comply with export-control rules on Russia  [51] , aligning Taiwan's leading chipmaker with Western sanctions. Foreign industrial capital is still committing to the mainland: Reuters, citing sources, reported Tesla planning a new Shanghai plant to more than double its China capacity  [52] .

Playbook ✓: Action: prefer onshore exposure such as ASHR, at 36.62 USD, over offshore internet such as KWEB, at 34.10 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Trigger: a two-sessions growth target and fiscal package that confirms the easing bias  [38] . What changes the call: Western moves toward secondary sanctions on Chinese banks that facilitate Russian trade, or a default chain spreading from private developers to state-linked ones. ⚠ Divergence: policy is easing and the Shanghai Composite is stable, yet Tencent fell 9.79% in five sessions and private developers keep defaulting, so the easing has not reached the assets global investors actually own.

Macro Stance: Japan imports the energy shock with a central bank still anchored at zero. The Nikkei 225 closed at 26,476.50 index points, up 1.95% on Friday but down 2.78% over five sessions and 1.98% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Reuters reported consumer inflation in the capital perking up, with the Ukraine crisis set to add pressure  [53] , and The Japan Times reported the country bracing for even higher inflation  [54] . Mixed: imported inflation squeezes real incomes faster than it changes policy, although Reuters noted a board reshuffle may open scope for a less dovish BOJ  [55] .

Activity & Currency: Momentum was fading before the war. CNBC reported February factory growth falling to a five-month low  [56] , after a GDP rebound that, per The Guardian Nigeria News, came before the Omicron wave hit  [57] . With the BOJ pinned near zero while the Fed prepares to hike, the rate gap should keep the yen soft, turning dearer oil into a larger domestic cost; The Japan Times framed the war as a threat to the world's economic recovery  [58] . Friday's equity rebound was led by chip equipment and SoftBank: Tokyo Electron rose 5.79% to 56,600.00 JPY, Advantest 7.71% to 9,220.00 JPY and SoftBank Group 5.56% to 5,069.00 JPY, while Toyota, at 2,104.00 JPY, is down 5.29% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Regional security remains a second risk premium after DW reported North Korea firing a ballistic missile  [59] .

Playbook ✓: Action: keep Japan at neutral through EWJ, at 63.55 USD and up 1.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), tilted toward exporters with pricing power and semiconductor equipment rather than energy-importing domestic names. Trigger: a BOJ signal that tolerates higher yields would favour Japanese banks and weigh on the weak-yen exporter trade. What changes the call: a further leg up in oil that pushes Tokyo-style price gains into wages, a risk that grows with the war's economic consequences, which The Japan Times has set out  [60] .

Macro Stance: Australia is cushioned by commodities and constrained by cost-of-living politics. The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 6,997.80 index points, up 0.10% on Friday, down 3.10% over five sessions and up 0.14% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), after ABC reported a $74b one-day wipe-out followed by a rebound  [61] . The RBA's line, per WSJ, is that it will not follow the Fed on rate increases  [62] . Mixed: terms of trade improve, but households pay for the energy shock.

Demand & Financing: The AFR reported the last CPI spike at 3.5 per cent  [63] , yet ABC reported wages recording their worst result in seven years  [64] , which is the RBA's reason to wait. The labour market keeps tightening, as ABC's analysis of the falling unemployment rate shows  [65] , and financing costs are edging up at the margin, with ANZ lifting rates on some lending and savings accounts  [66] . ABC warned the invasion drives up energy costs Australians will not escape  [67] . Iron ore is the swing factor: The Australian reported China threatening an iron ore single market  [68] , and BHP closed at 39.79 AUD, down 6.82% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).

Playbook ✓: Action: favour resources outside the China iron-ore channel, such as Lynas, which rose 6.93% to 9.57 AUD on Friday, over the major banks, with CBA at 93.88 AUD and down 3.96% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Trigger: an RBA shift away from patience if wages break higher. What changes the call: Chinese purchasing controls that cap iron ore, which would hit BHP and Fortescue, at 18.60 AUD, harder than domestic rate risk.

Macro Stance: Poland enters the week as NATO's frontline economy with inflation already at its highest of this century, per SII's reading of the January data  [69] . Forsal.pl reported GUS putting January inflation at 9.2%  [70] , and Rzeczpospolita reported the RPP lifting rates to their highest in almost nine years  [71] . Rzeczpospolita summarised the invasion's consequences as higher inflation and a weaker zloty  [72] , the worst mix for a central bank still catching up. The labour market is turning at the margin: Obserwator Gospodarczy reported unemployment rising for the first time in almost a year  [73] . The structural support has been labour supply; INNPoland argued that without Ukrainians Poland's high GDP growth would be a dream  [74] , and war is now reshaping that pool. Bearish on duration and the currency, selective on equities.

Markets: Friday brought what Bankier called a historic rebound on the GPW, with banks coming to the rescue of the WIG20  [75] , a day after a war-panic crash  [76] . The Beta ETF WIG20TR closed at 33.93 PLN, up 7.71% on Friday but down 8.30% over five sessions and 9.81% over 20; PKO Bank Polski rose 13.27% to 40.72 PLN, Bank Pekao 17.14% to 118.60 PLN and mBank 12.81% to 389.20 PLN, yet mBank is still down 14.16% over five sessions, and the dollar-based EPOL closed at 18.45 USD, down 10.35% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The currency is the weak point: Forbes listed the zloty among the biggest losers of the war's outbreak  [77] , and Rzeczpospolita said it was the cheapest in months  [78] . Business Insider Polska reported Poles withdrawing more cash, as at the start of the pandemic  [79] , while the NBP said its cash reserves are sufficient  [80] .

Fiscal & Politics: Security is now a fiscal line item. Bankier reported the government adopting the draft homeland-defence act and asked whether NBP profit will finance the armed forces  [81] , on top of pandemic spending that Rzeczpospolita said reached a record  [82] , and the World Bank's Poland public finance review  [83]  sets the fiscal backdrop for the trade-offs. Tax politics remain messy: Money.pl reported more than a hundred thousand Poles losing money because Polski Ład did not account for them  [84] , after Biznes Wprost reported dismissals at the finance ministry over the reform  [85] . The anti-inflation shield is under strain at the pump, with Fakt warning of fuel at 6 zł and asking whether the government shield has stopped working  [86] , while TVN24 reported UOKiK will police fuel prices as Orlen cuts ties with stations that inflated them  [87] . naTemat reported the PiS government demanding 'crushing' sanctions on Russia  [88] .

Corporate & Sectors: The corporate map splits on Ukraine exposure and commodity leverage. Rzeczpospolita reported Orlen introducing refuelling limits  [89] , Bankier reported it terminating contracts while imposing limits  [90]  and later that it had increased deliveries to the east where fuel ran short  [91] ; wnp.pl reported Russian crude is less than half of its refinery runs  [92] . Orlen rose 10.96% to 69.86 PLN on Friday. LPP, which closed its Ukrainian stores and moved its Kyiv office to Lviv according to Wiadomości Handlowe  [93] , closed at 9,590.00 PLN, down 36.07% over five sessions, and Allegro, which Strefa Inwestorów said posted record fourth-quarter revenue but disappointing profitability  [94] , closed at 27.51 PLN, down 15.74% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Bankier reported Allegro CEO Francois Nuyts stepping down  [95] , and PKO BP's chief said the bank had prepared for every scenario at Kredobank in Ukraine  [96] . KGHM rose 9.34% to 155.70 PLN and JSW 9.80% to 41.80 PLN; Wyborcza reported KGHM and Orlen pursuing small modular reactors  [97] .

Geopolitics & Security: The security premium is being met with physical reinforcement. Notes From Poland reported the UK sending an advanced air-defence system  [98] , GOV.UK announced UK forces arriving on NATO's eastern flank  [99] , and Onet reported the Polish army raising combat readiness  [100] . Public opinion has shifted, with a Rzeczpospolita poll finding 71.1% of Poles think Russia could attack Poland  [101] , and Moscow has retaliated in the air, banning flights from Bulgaria, Poland and the Czech Republic, per Al Jazeera  [102] . Al Jazeera reported tens of thousands fleeing to Poland  [103] , and Radio-Canada reported officials pledging help to all Ukrainians fleeing the war  [104] , a humanitarian commitment with fiscal and housing costs. Energy routing is the other front: Reuters reported Yamal-Europe flows running east  [105] , raising the strategic value of Baltic Pipe, which WysokieNapiecie examined  [106] .

New / Most Important: The weekend validated Warsaw's hard line: CBC reported a widening group of countries moving to block Russian access to SWIFT  [7] , and POLITICO reported the EU agreeing €500M in arms and aid for Ukraine's military in a 'watershed' move  [107] . That makes Poland the logistics hub for Western support and a plausible target for Russian counter-measures. For the economy, Bankier's analysis that immigrants will first seek shelter before entering the labour market  [108]  implies a near-term cost to public finances ahead of any labour-supply dividend, while banks waiving fees for Ukrainians, per Business Insider Polska  [109] , is a small fee-income cost the sector is choosing to carry.

Playbook ✓: Action: stay underweight Polish duration and zloty-sensitive assets, and fade Friday's bank-led bounce rather than chase it; within equities prefer commodity exporters such as KGHM and JSW over discretionary names with Ukrainian store networks such as LPP. Trigger: a renewed slide in the WIG20TR tracker below Friday's 33.93 PLN close alongside further zloty weakness would confirm the risk premium is rebuilding. What changes the call: an RPP move large enough to stabilise the currency, or a negotiated ceasefire that restores value to Polish firms' Ukrainian businesses. ⚠ Divergence: domestic buyers stepped in hard on Friday, with PKO up 13.27% and Pekao up 17.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), and the NBP is publicly calming fears of cash-machine queues  [110] , so local positioning may already be cleaner than the currency's weakness implies.

Narrative: Technology was the fulcrum of the week's reversal, and YCharts was already asking how long tech stocks take to recover from a crash  [111] . XLK closed at 154.35 USD, up 1.36% on Friday and 1.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), yet Barron's still described a bear-market scare in tech  [112] . Balance sheets are the sector's defence, but it owns the most duration in a bear-flattening curve.

Reported: Nvidia's fourth-quarter release  [113]  remains the demand anchor, and Cisco raised its annual earnings forecast alongside $15 bln of buybacks  [114] . Dell was the miss: Investor's Business Daily reported the stock tumbling after the company missed its earnings goal  [115] , and it fell 7.84% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).

EPS Upside Watch: Apple is the upside case. Counterpoint reported Apple capturing its highest-ever smartphone share in the fourth quarter of a record ~$450 billion revenue year  [116] , and AAPL closed at 164.85 USD, up 3.54% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Cybersecurity is trading like defence. Palo Alto Networks closed at 569.75 USD, up 14.15% over five sessions, as Fox News warned Russian cyberattacks could come to the US  [117] . Treat security software as a war hedge, not generic growth.

Narrative: Communication services is where sanctions policy meets platform economics. XLC closed at 68.53 USD, down 2.52% over 20 sessions, and Meta Platforms (FB) at 210.48 USD, down 28.56% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Reuters reported Meta barring Russian state media from running ads  [118]  and Google blocking RT and other Russian channels from earning ad dollars  [119] : compliance now has a revenue cost.

Reported: Roblox suffered its worst post-earnings drop, per Bloomberg  [120] ; Nexstar reported fourth-quarter net revenue of $1.25 billion  [121] ; and The Hollywood Reporter's studio profit report had Disney diving while Sony soared  [122] .

EPS Upside Watch: Meta's Reels push is the swing factor for FB. Reuters reported the global launch of its 'fastest growing' format  [123] , and Ad Age reported new creator ad features aimed at TikTok  [124] . Upside requires Reels monetisation to close the gap with feed advertising before engagement shifts further.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Content moderation has become a geopolitical liability as well as a brand risk. Reuters' focus on Spotify's Joe Rogan saga spotlighted podcast moderation challenges  [125] ; SPOT closed at 151.91 USD, down 11.33% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).

Narrative: Financials rallied on Friday, with XLF up 3.22% to 39.10 USD and KRE up 4.60% to 73.84 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), but the weekend shifted the debate to sanctions plumbing. Kharon reported Sberbank landing on a rare US Treasury list  [126] , and the Los Angeles Times asked how American financial institutions will deal with Russia sanctions  [127] .

Reported: Canadian banks are the template: Reuters reported CIBC and National Bank beating estimates on lending and markets units  [128] , while RBC's profit rise came with a mortgage-slowdown flag  [129] . Rocket Companies reported lower earnings but issued a special dividend  [130] .

EPS Upside Watch: The 2Y's 37 bps rise over 20 observations lifts asset yields, but the 21 bps compression in 10Y-2Y caps margins (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25); Kansas City Fed research asking whether margins at small and large banks respond differently to rates  [131]  is the right lens; asset-sensitive regionals benefit most.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Regulation, not credit, is the brokers' near-term risk. The Financial Times reported Morgan Stanley disclosing twin probes into big stock transactions  [132] , and Reuters reported an SEC investigation of Goldman Sachs over employee communications  [133] . MS closed at 94.55 USD, down 6.52% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).

Narrative: Energy prices supply risk, but not fully. Brent closed at 97.93 USD/bbl and WTI at 91.59 USD/bbl, down 1.16% and 1.31% on Friday after Reuters reported oil topping $105 on the invasion  [134] ; Brent is still up 9.61% over 20 sessions and XLE up 4.51% at 68.88 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Time explained why sanctions are not targeting oil and gas  [135] , hence Friday's dip.

Reported: CNBC reported BP offloading its nearly 20% stake in Rosneft  [136]  after WSJ reported UK government pressure  [137] . ExxonMobil agreed to sell its Nigerian shallow-water affiliate  [138] , and Reuters reported its workforce falling by 9,000 in 2021 amid cost cuts  [139] .

EPS Upside Watch: Chevron said it is monitoring Russia and can adjust crude supply  [140] ; CVX closed at 140.38 USD, up 5.07% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). US majors keep operating leverage to price; the debate is how much windfall boards return.

⚡ Breaking Convention: US gas tells a different story: Henry Hub closed at 4.47 USD/MMBtu, down 28.65% over 20 sessions, while TTF rose 26.04% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The transatlantic gap is a call option on US export capacity rather than on domestic prices.

Narrative: Defence has moved from hedge to budget line. POLITICO described Germany's historic shift to ramp up defence spending  [141] , and ITA closed at 107.63 USD, up 8.92% over 20 sessions, with Northrop Grumman up 9.54% and Raytheon Technologies (RTX) up 9.90% to 98.12 USD, while XLI rose only 0.12% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).

Reported: BAE Systems published full-year results  [142]  and said, per Reuters, that the invasion will sharpen the focus on defence  [143] . Deere's price hikes powered an earnings beat  [144] , yet DE fell 8.82% over five sessions to 346.98 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).

EPS Upside Watch: Lockheed Martin rose 5.33% over five sessions to 409.49 USD and General Dynamics 6.33% to 227.98 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25); GovCon Wire reported a $108M Electric Boat maintenance award for General Dynamics  [145] . European budget increases should feed US primes' export books with a lag.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Aerospace supply chains are the hidden war exposure. Bloomberg reported jet-engine makers looking for titanium outside Russia  [146] , and Reuters reported Safran boosting titanium stocks  [147] . Boeing fell 5.67% over five sessions to 201.48 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), and Reuters reported airlines tackling widening Russia risks  [148] .

Narrative: Consumer discretionary is most exposed to the energy tax on households. XLY closed at 176.19 USD, down 2.72% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), and ABC7 reported pump prices rising as President Biden promised to soften the blow  [149] . Falling real incomes hit big-ticket and home categories first.

Reported: Home Depot beat estimates and sees sales growth, per CNBC  [150] , but Reuters flagged its margin warning  [151] ; HD fell 8.99% over five sessions to 316.65 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). TJX missed on Omicron store closures  [152] , and Foot Locker's 2022 forecast was hit by Nike's shift  [153] .

EPS Upside Watch: Carvana is the idiosyncratic upside: TechCrunch reported its $2.2B purchase of the Adesa US auction business  [154] , and CVNA jumped 21.04% to 152.57 USD on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Lowe's struck an optimistic tone on home-improvement demand despite rising rates  [155] .

⚡ Breaking Convention: Tesla's discount is governance as much as demand. WSJ reported an SEC probe into trading by Elon Musk and his brother after the CEO's share sales  [156] , and TSLA fell 7.59% over five sessions to 809.87 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).

Buffett called Apple one of the Four Giants driving Berkshire's value  [258] , and Forbes Middle East puts Berkshire's 2021 net profit at $89.8B  [257] , numbers that read like a fortress. The letter came out on Saturday, after an invasion week that ended with the S&P 500 up 2.24% on Friday at 4,384.65 index points and the VIX down 2.73 points to 27.59, while Apple rose 1.30% to $164.85 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Then the weekend escalated: the US and Europe moved to bar some Russian banks from SWIFT  [3]  and Germany committed €100 billion to defence  [21] .

The Social Signal: The attention is broad for a shareholder letter, and it is the copy-the-master kind. MoneyWise was already walking readers through four of Buffett's most notable fourth-quarter portfolio changes  [264] , Yahoo Finance is running a piece on Buffett's fourth law of motion  [265] , and Time led with the mildly attractive path of $27 billion in buybacks  [241] . The same weekend, CNBC asked readers whether they panic sold during the week's volatility and when to get back into the market  [244] . The pattern implies a crowd looking for permission to stay invested, and Berkshire's letter is the most trusted permission slip on offer.

Historical Analog: The analog the Buffett crowd reaches for is Buffett himself. CNBC's read before the letter was that for Berkshire the big issues haven't changed  [266] , and Business Insider's reminder that Buffett avoids Russia over threats of violence and asset seizure  [267]  looks, after a week of sanctions, like the old discipline paying off in plain sight. The mechanism is the anti-meme. Berkshire compounds through cash-generating businesses and buys itself back when nothing better is on offer, so it is built to look dull in manias and sturdy in drawdowns. Over 20 sessions the stock is up 3.76% against 1.34% for the S&P 500 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), a margin made of patience rather than leverage.

Smart Money View: Here the smart money is the letter, and it is less bullish than the crowd's reading. Reuters says Buffett lamented a lack of good investments even as Berkshire's profit set a record  [256] ; a manager who laments a shortage of good investments is not calling a bottom. The bull reading has support too, since CNBC frames Apple as one of the Four Giants driving Berkshire's value  [258] , and Business Insider's account of Buffett blasting fake earnings  [259]  can be read as a jab at the profitless growth stories retail chased in 2021. And Payments Industry Intelligence's explanation of why Berkshire sold out of Visa and Mastercard  [268]  is a reminder that Buffett sells as readily as he buys.

When the Narrative Breaks: The trade breaks if safe turns out to mean already priced. Buffett's own framing, buybacks on a merely mildly attractive path  [241]  alongside the lament about a lack of good investments, implies Berkshire sees its stock as fair rather than cheap, so Friday's 3.56% jump leaves less margin than believers assume. The observable line is the $307.67 close of twenty sessions earlier: a slide back there while the S&P 500 holds would say the letter bought no premium at all (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Concentration is the second trigger, because an Apple drawdown hits one of the Four Giants directly. And Monday opens on a weekend of SWIFT exclusions; a market that lurches lower will test whether retail holds Berkshire as a haven or sells it as a source of cash.

Why Retail Is Here: The war trade just found a sovereign customer. Germany committed €100 billion to defence spending  [21] , with Scholz framing the increase as a response to Putin's war  [22]  and POLITICO calling it a historic shift  [141] . Rheinmetall had already closed Friday at €107.05, up 7.00% on the day, 11.00% over five sessions and 15.06% over twenty (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), and US contractors moved with it, Lockheed Martin up 3.48% to $409.49 and Raytheon Technologies 4.11%. For the crowd that cheered war-friendly stocks on invasion day  [269] , this is confirmation: the trade now has a budget behind it.

Where It Breaks: A pledge is not a purchase order. The money still has to become contracts, procurement runs on years rather than weekends, and the risk for late buyers is paying for a decade of orders in a single gap. The BBC calls it a dramatic German U-turn  [217] ; the larger the turn, the longer the road from announcement to delivery. Watch the €93.04 close of twenty sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25): the further the shares run above it on promises alone, the more any delay in turning the pledge into orders would hurt.

Why Retail Is Here: Block is the crowd's fintech, the payments name CNBC traces from a scrappy hardware start-up to a powerhouse  [253] , and after a brutal stretch for fintech it delivered the day believers wait for. Australian holders got there first, with ABC reporting Block soaring on the ASX  [61] ; then the US shares rose 26.14% to $119.82 on Friday, the first session after quarterly results in which, Payments Dive reports, the company defended higher marketing spending  [198] . They are now up 15.19% over five sessions and 13.42% over twenty, and PayPal rose 5.64% the same day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The emotional pull is the comeback: a name left for dead jumps by a quarter in a day, and every holder who stayed feels vindicated.

Where It Breaks: The bear case sits inside the same results: that marketing push  [198]  means part of the growth is being bought. The sector has not been forgiven, only Block's quarter, with PayPal still down 29.83% and Affirm 23.17% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). A slide back toward the $105.64 close of twenty sessions earlier would make Friday look like a relief burst rather than a new trend, and with the 2Y yield up 37 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25), rates are no friend to a re-rating.

Why Retail Is Here: The war has turned supply chains into a national-security story, and a US rare-earth miner is its simplest ticker. MP Materials reported higher profit as rare-earth prices surged  [170] , days after announcing a Department of Defense heavy rare-earth processing contract  [270] . The stock rose 6.84% to $46.85 on Friday, 12.62% over five sessions and 25.10% over twenty, and Australia's Lynas Rare Earths gained 6.93% to A$9.57 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The crowd's pitch is simple: if the West cannot rely on hostile suppliers, the domestic miner becomes strategic, and strategic assets get bid.

Where It Breaks: The bid is a bet on prices staying high and governments staying generous. A 25.10% run in twenty sessions prices in a lot of both, and a commodity producer's earnings swing with the very rare-earth prices that just made the quarter. The Statesman's warning that the war could worsen the global chip shortage  [191]  cuts both ways, because the end markets for magnets need chips too. Watch the $37.45 close of twenty sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25): a fade back toward it would say the security premium was a headline trade, not a re-rating.

geo.label: Fed lift-off intact into a war shock
parts: Macro Stance

Friday's violent relief rally has already been partly overtaken. The S&P 500 closed at 4,384.65 index points (+2.24% on the day, +0.10% over five sessions) and the Nasdaq 100 at 14,189.16 index points (+1.53%), while the VIX fell 2.73 points to 27.59 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Reuters framed it as investors digesting sanctions on Russia [[n1223]], after Fortune described the week's reversal as one of the incredible vaults in equity-market history [[n0121]]. That rally priced the first sanctions package; The New York Times then reported the US and Europe will bar some Russian banks from SWIFT [[n1412]]. Mixed: US earnings are less exposed than Europe's, but multiples rest on a Fed that experts quoted by Business Insider say will not rescue a meltdown [[n0803]].
Rates & Curve

The curve says the Fed matters more than the war. The 2Y closed at 1.55% and the 10Y at 1.97%, leaving 10Y-2Y at +42 bps, with the 3M at 0.33% and 10Y-3M at +164 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25). Over 20 observations the 2Y rose 37 bps from 1.18% and the 10Y 16 bps from 1.81%, so the spread compressed by 21 bps: the curve is positively sloped and the 20-observation move is a bear flattening, both up with the 2Y up more. Over five observations the 2Y added 6 bps and the 10Y was unchanged, meaning the safe-haven bid Reuters described on invasion day [[n0208]] only anchored the long end. Xinhua reported a Fed official signalling a March hike remains on track despite Ukraine [[n2180]].
New / Most Important

Two shifts matter. First, the SWIFT step, which CBC said Canada is joining [[n1416]], moves sanctions from named lenders to the payment rails, raising settlement risk for anyone still clearing Russian flows. Second, demand was already softening: The Conference Board said consumer confidence declined for a second consecutive month in February [[n2087]], and Builder reported pending home sales falling for a third straight month in January [[n2110]], against the largest annual consumer-price gain in 40 years [[n2032]]. Corporate cash is going to buybacks, with CNBC reporting a record $27 billion Berkshire repurchase in 2021 [[n0806]]. The DXY slipped 0.54% to 96.62 index points on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25) after Reuters had reported the dollar near a two-year high on invasion day [[n1210]].
Playbook ✓

Action: hold US quality large caps and energy over long-duration growth, and keep index hedges on while the VIX sits at 27.59 index points. Trigger to add risk: the S&P 500 holding Friday's 4,384.65 close as markets absorb the SWIFT measures, with the VIX failing to regain 30.49, its late-January level (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). What changes the call: a front end that keeps rising while the 10Y stalls would deepen the bear flattening from +42 bps and signal tightening into a growth shock; Reuters has already reported louder calls for 50 bps rather than 25 bps in March [[n2040]]. The State of the Union on March 1 [[n0118]] tests whether Washington pairs sanctions with energy-price relief.

geo.label: ECB taper meets energy shock
parts: Macro Stance

Europe is where the weekend's escalation lands hardest. Friday's bounce lifted the STOXX 600 3.32% to 453.53 index points and the DAX 3.67% to 14,567.23 index points, yet both remain down 2.58% and 4.91% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Since then Europe has moved to remove Russian banks from SWIFT, per Global Finance [[n1226]], and to shut its airspace to Russian airlines while funding weapons purchases for Ukraine, per PBS [[n1225]]. Bearish: the region carries the energy, banking and trade exposure that sanctions and counter-sanctions now target.
Activity & Inflation

The growth starting point was respectable, with Times of Malta reporting euro-zone growth jumping as virus restrictions eased [[n1144]]. The price side is the problem: Eurostat put energy inflation at 27% [[n1220]], and The Guardian argued the war will fuel a sharp further hike [[n1222]]. Dutch TTF gas closed at 94.42 EUR/MWh, down 29.70% on Friday but up 26.04% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), a volatility profile that makes industrial hedging expensive. ECB policymakers told Reuters not to go back on quicker taper plans [[n1224]], so the stagflation trade-off is live.
New / Most Important

Germany's U-turn is the regime change. DW reported a €100 billion commitment to defence spending [[n1228]], Reuters quoted Scholz calling it a response to 'Putin's war' [[n1229]], and Clean Energy Wire reported plans for strategic gas and coal reserves [[n1221]]. Fiscal expansion for security and energy storage is inflationary at the margin, supportive for defence and grid suppliers, and a direct cost to taxpayers.
Playbook ✓

Action: underweight euro-area banks with Russian subsidiaries and energy-intensive cyclicals; overweight defence. Societe Generale closed at 28.45 EUR, down 12.09% over five sessions, while Rheinmetall closed at 107.05 EUR, up 11.00% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Trigger: add to the bank underweight if TTF rebuilds Friday's 29.70% drop. What changes the call: a credible negotiation track that takes TTF back below 92.30 EUR/MWh, its late-January level, which would ease the margin squeeze on industry and the inflation pressure on the ECB.

geo.label: Easing bias, offshore discount
parts: Macro Stance

China is trading as a policy-insulated onshore market and a sanctions-sensitive offshore one. The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,451.41 index points, up 0.63% on Friday and down only 1.13% over five sessions, while the Hang Seng closed at 22,767.18 index points, down 6.41% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Beijing's line, which PBS described as avoiding criticism of the Russian attack while calling for talks [[n1350]], keeps it outside the Western coalition; The New York Times reported US officials had repeatedly urged China to help avert the war [[n1395]]. Mixed: onshore policy support is real, but the offshore market is pricing regulatory and geopolitical risk at the same time.
PMIs & Activity

The last private factory gauge was weak: Reuters reported January Caixin activity contracting as COVID lockdowns bit [[n0139]]. Against that, China Daily reported industrial profits rebounding in 2021 as production improved [[n0137]], and Best Selling Cars Blog put January vehicle wholesales up 0.9% in a stable market [[n0162]]. Structural drags show up regionally, with SCMP reporting a rust-belt province unveiling a population plan in the face of economic decline [[n0185]]. Power investment is the bright spot: Global Times reported an expected record 75-90GW of solar additions [[n0181]]. The next activity readings are the February surveys; until then the read is soft manufacturing and policy-led investment.
Credit Impulse

The policy direction is easier even before the credit numbers confirm it. Reuters reported that slowing inflation leaves room for policy easing [[n0149]], and Bloomberg described the People's Bank seizing the moment for stimulus as the Fed hikes [[n0134]]. That divergence is the core of the China call: the US 2Y has risen 37 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25) while Beijing leans the other way. The constraint is transmission through a stressed property sector and a tighter grip on platform finance; The Japan Times reported regulators telling banks and state firms to report exposure to Jack Ma's Ant [[n0161]]. Easing channelled through state lenders and infrastructure should lift onshore equities before it lifts household consumption.
Property

Property is still triage rather than recovery. Reuters reported Evergrande selling four projects to state-owned firms for $337 mln [[n0220]], and SCMP described Chinese firms picking away at its assets [[n0228]]. CNBC reported Moody's downgrading Shimao as debt troubles drag on [[n0205]], and The Standard reported Fantasia being sued over its bond default [[n0170]]. The pattern is a controlled transfer of viable projects into state hands, which limits systemic contagion but leaves private developers' offshore bondholders at the back of the queue. For equities, it means the property drag on steel, building materials and household wealth persists even as policy eases at the margin.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

The next policy signal is the annual 'two sessions', which SCMP previewed as Beijing plotting its course [[n0212]]; the growth target and fiscal quota will set the tone for the quarter. Hong Kong is already spending, with Al Jazeera reporting a $22bn budget as zero-COVID hammers businesses [[n0187]]. Trade cuts both ways. Reuters reported Russia's trade flows shifting towards China as sanctions start [[n1281]], and Global Times quoted analysts saying the agricultural-trade impact on China is limited [[n0209]]. Doubts over the phase-one deal, which SCMP asked was a 'historic failure' [[n0233]], and the Peterson Institute's finding that China bought none of the extra $200 billion of US exports [[n0145]] make secondary measures a tail risk if Beijing is seen to cushion Moscow.
Markets & Flows

Offshore internet is where the discount is applied. Tencent closed at 402.71 HKD, down 9.79% over five sessions, and Alibaba's Hong Kong line at 105.30 HKD, down 11.88%, while KWEB fell 9.04% and FXI 6.80% over the same span; ASHR, the onshore CSI 300 proxy, rose 0.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Reuters tied the rout to fresh fears of a regulatory crackdown [[n0171]], and Bloomberg reported Alibaba planning for a new normal of low growth [[n0196]]. Primary-market appetite has faded too: Reuters reported Shein shelving its US IPO plan again on uncertain markets [[n1259]], and WSJ reported a US block-trading investigation hitting Morgan Stanley's plans to expand in China [[n0225]]. The yuan is the counterpoint, with China Daily arguing it will remain an investor safe haven [[n0218]].
New / Most Important

The war has sharpened the Taiwan question for portfolios. Reuters reported Beijing insisting Taiwan is 'not Ukraine' as the island raised its alert level [[n1320]], and separately Taiwan warning of Chinese aircraft in its air defence zone [[n1371]]. TSMC said it will comply with export-control rules on Russia [[n0653]], aligning Taiwan's leading chipmaker with Western sanctions. Foreign industrial capital is still committing to the mainland: Reuters, citing sources, reported Tesla planning a new Shanghai plant to more than double its China capacity [[n1913]].
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer onshore exposure such as ASHR, at 36.62 USD, over offshore internet such as KWEB, at 34.10 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Trigger: a two-sessions growth target and fiscal package that confirms the easing bias [[n0212]]. What changes the call: Western moves toward secondary sanctions on Chinese banks that facilitate Russian trade, or a default chain spreading from private developers to state-linked ones. ⚠ Divergence: policy is easing and the Shanghai Composite is stable, yet Tencent fell 9.79% in five sessions and private developers keep defaulting, so the easing has not reached the assets global investors actually own.

geo.label: BOJ patient, imported inflation
parts: Macro Stance

Japan imports the energy shock with a central bank still anchored at zero. The Nikkei 225 closed at 26,476.50 index points, up 1.95% on Friday but down 2.78% over five sessions and 1.98% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Reuters reported consumer inflation in the capital perking up, with the Ukraine crisis set to add pressure [[n1048]], and The Japan Times reported the country bracing for even higher inflation [[n1463]]. Mixed: imported inflation squeezes real incomes faster than it changes policy, although Reuters noted a board reshuffle may open scope for a less dovish BOJ [[n1435]].
Activity & Currency

Momentum was fading before the war. CNBC reported February factory growth falling to a five-month low [[n1437]], after a GDP rebound that, per The Guardian Nigeria News, came before the Omicron wave hit [[n1433]]. With the BOJ pinned near zero while the Fed prepares to hike, the rate gap should keep the yen soft, turning dearer oil into a larger domestic cost; The Japan Times framed the war as a threat to the world's economic recovery [[n1462]]. Friday's equity rebound was led by chip equipment and SoftBank: Tokyo Electron rose 5.79% to 56,600.00 JPY, Advantest 7.71% to 9,220.00 JPY and SoftBank Group 5.56% to 5,069.00 JPY, while Toyota, at 2,104.00 JPY, is down 5.29% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Regional security remains a second risk premium after DW reported North Korea firing a ballistic missile [[n1417]].
Playbook ✓

Action: keep Japan at neutral through EWJ, at 63.55 USD and up 1.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), tilted toward exporters with pricing power and semiconductor equipment rather than energy-importing domestic names. Trigger: a BOJ signal that tolerates higher yields would favour Japanese banks and weigh on the weak-yen exporter trade. What changes the call: a further leg up in oil that pushes Tokyo-style price gains into wages, a risk that grows with the war's economic consequences, which The Japan Times has set out [[n1472]].

geo.label: RBA patient, commodity cushion
parts: Macro Stance

Australia is cushioned by commodities and constrained by cost-of-living politics. The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 6,997.80 index points, up 0.10% on Friday, down 3.10% over five sessions and up 0.14% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), after ABC reported a $74b one-day wipe-out followed by a rebound [[n0061]]. The RBA's line, per WSJ, is that it will not follow the Fed on rate increases [[n0025]]. Mixed: terms of trade improve, but households pay for the energy shock.
Demand & Financing

The AFR reported the last CPI spike at 3.5 per cent [[n0004]], yet ABC reported wages recording their worst result in seven years [[n0073]], which is the RBA's reason to wait. The labour market keeps tightening, as ABC's analysis of the falling unemployment rate shows [[n0087]], and financing costs are edging up at the margin, with ANZ lifting rates on some lending and savings accounts [[n0060]]. ABC warned the invasion drives up energy costs Australians will not escape [[n0081]]. Iron ore is the swing factor: The Australian reported China threatening an iron ore single market [[n0037]], and BHP closed at 39.79 AUD, down 6.82% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
Playbook ✓

Action: favour resources outside the China iron-ore channel, such as Lynas, which rose 6.93% to 9.57 AUD on Friday, over the major banks, with CBA at 93.88 AUD and down 3.96% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Trigger: an RBA shift away from patience if wages break higher. What changes the call: Chinese purchasing controls that cap iron ore, which would hit BHP and Fortescue, at 18.60 AUD, harder than domestic rate risk.

geo.label: NBP tightening on the frontline
parts: Macro Stance

Poland enters the week as NATO's frontline economy with inflation already at its highest of this century, per SII's reading of the January data [[n1537]]. Forsal.pl reported GUS putting January inflation at 9.2% [[n1536]], and Rzeczpospolita reported the RPP lifting rates to their highest in almost nine years [[n1531]]. Rzeczpospolita summarised the invasion's consequences as higher inflation and a weaker zloty [[n1666]], the worst mix for a central bank still catching up. The labour market is turning at the margin: Obserwator Gospodarczy reported unemployment rising for the first time in almost a year [[n1625]]. The structural support has been labour supply; INNPoland argued that without Ukrainians Poland's high GDP growth would be a dream [[n1621]], and war is now reshaping that pool. Bearish on duration and the currency, selective on equities.
Markets

Friday brought what Bankier called a historic rebound on the GPW, with banks coming to the rescue of the WIG20 [[n1694]], a day after a war-panic crash [[n1646]]. The Beta ETF WIG20TR closed at 33.93 PLN, up 7.71% on Friday but down 8.30% over five sessions and 9.81% over 20; PKO Bank Polski rose 13.27% to 40.72 PLN, Bank Pekao 17.14% to 118.60 PLN and mBank 12.81% to 389.20 PLN, yet mBank is still down 14.16% over five sessions, and the dollar-based EPOL closed at 18.45 USD, down 10.35% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The currency is the weak point: Forbes listed the zloty among the biggest losers of the war's outbreak [[n1729]], and Rzeczpospolita said it was the cheapest in months [[n1681]]. Business Insider Polska reported Poles withdrawing more cash, as at the start of the pandemic [[n1653]], while the NBP said its cash reserves are sufficient [[n1702]].
Fiscal & Politics

Security is now a fiscal line item. Bankier reported the government adopting the draft homeland-defence act and asked whether NBP profit will finance the armed forces [[n1590]], on top of pandemic spending that Rzeczpospolita said reached a record [[n1583]], and the World Bank's Poland public finance review [[n1485]] sets the fiscal backdrop for the trade-offs. Tax politics remain messy: Money.pl reported more than a hundred thousand Poles losing money because Polski Ład did not account for them [[n1747]], after Biznes Wprost reported dismissals at the finance ministry over the reform [[n1548]]. The anti-inflation shield is under strain at the pump, with Fakt warning of fuel at 6 zł and asking whether the government shield has stopped working [[n1749]], while TVN24 reported UOKiK will police fuel prices as Orlen cuts ties with stations that inflated them [[n1724]]. naTemat reported the PiS government demanding 'crushing' sanctions on Russia [[n1741]].
Corporate & Sectors

The corporate map splits on Ukraine exposure and commodity leverage. Rzeczpospolita reported Orlen introducing refuelling limits [[n1712]], Bankier reported it terminating contracts while imposing limits [[n1688]] and later that it had increased deliveries to the east where fuel ran short [[n1744]]; wnp.pl reported Russian crude is less than half of its refinery runs [[n1672]]. Orlen rose 10.96% to 69.86 PLN on Friday. LPP, which closed its Ukrainian stores and moved its Kyiv office to Lviv according to Wiadomości Handlowe [[n1665]], closed at 9,590.00 PLN, down 36.07% over five sessions, and Allegro, which Strefa Inwestorów said posted record fourth-quarter revenue but disappointing profitability [[n1687]], closed at 27.51 PLN, down 15.74% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Bankier reported Allegro CEO Francois Nuyts stepping down [[n1640]], and PKO BP's chief said the bank had prepared for every scenario at Kredobank in Ukraine [[n1656]]. KGHM rose 9.34% to 155.70 PLN and JSW 9.80% to 41.80 PLN; Wyborcza reported KGHM and Orlen pursuing small modular reactors [[n1734]].
Geopolitics & Security

The security premium is being met with physical reinforcement. Notes From Poland reported the UK sending an advanced air-defence system [[n1492]], GOV.UK announced UK forces arriving on NATO's eastern flank [[n1507]], and Onet reported the Polish army raising combat readiness [[n1673]]. Public opinion has shifted, with a Rzeczpospolita poll finding 71.1% of Poles think Russia could attack Poland [[n1667]], and Moscow has retaliated in the air, banning flights from Bulgaria, Poland and the Czech Republic, per Al Jazeera [[n1506]]. Al Jazeera reported tens of thousands fleeing to Poland [[n1509]], and Radio-Canada reported officials pledging help to all Ukrainians fleeing the war [[n1497]], a humanitarian commitment with fiscal and housing costs. Energy routing is the other front: Reuters reported Yamal-Europe flows running east [[n1480]], raising the strategic value of Baltic Pipe, which WysokieNapiecie examined [[n1547]].
New / Most Important

The weekend validated Warsaw's hard line: CBC reported a widening group of countries moving to block Russian access to SWIFT [[n1416]], and POLITICO reported the EU agreeing €500M in arms and aid for Ukraine's military in a 'watershed' move [[n1511]]. That makes Poland the logistics hub for Western support and a plausible target for Russian counter-measures. For the economy, Bankier's analysis that immigrants will first seek shelter before entering the labour market [[n1726]] implies a near-term cost to public finances ahead of any labour-supply dividend, while banks waiving fees for Ukrainians, per Business Insider Polska [[n1746]], is a small fee-income cost the sector is choosing to carry.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight Polish duration and zloty-sensitive assets, and fade Friday's bank-led bounce rather than chase it; within equities prefer commodity exporters such as KGHM and JSW over discretionary names with Ukrainian store networks such as LPP. Trigger: a renewed slide in the WIG20TR tracker below Friday's 33.93 PLN close alongside further zloty weakness would confirm the risk premium is rebuilding. What changes the call: an RPP move large enough to stabilise the currency, or a negotiated ceasefire that restores value to Polish firms' Ukrainian businesses. ⚠ Divergence: domestic buyers stepped in hard on Friday, with PKO up 13.27% and Pekao up 17.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), and the NBP is publicly calming fears of cash-machine queues [[n1698]], so local positioning may already be cleaner than the currency's weakness implies.
Narrative

Technology was the fulcrum of the week's reversal, and YCharts was already asking how long tech stocks take to recover from a crash [[n1916]]. XLK closed at 154.35 USD, up 1.36% on Friday and 1.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), yet Barron's still described a bear-market scare in tech [[n0776]]. Balance sheets are the sector's defence, but it owns the most duration in a bear-flattening curve.
Reported

Nvidia's fourth-quarter release [[n0965]] remains the demand anchor, and Cisco raised its annual earnings forecast alongside $15 bln of buybacks [[n0962]]. Dell was the miss: Investor's Business Daily reported the stock tumbling after the company missed its earnings goal [[n0714]], and it fell 7.84% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
EPS Upside Watch

Apple is the upside case. Counterpoint reported Apple capturing its highest-ever smartphone share in the fourth quarter of a record ~$450 billion revenue year [[n1052]], and AAPL closed at 164.85 USD, up 3.54% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Cybersecurity is trading like defence. Palo Alto Networks closed at 569.75 USD, up 14.15% over five sessions, as Fox News warned Russian cyberattacks could come to the US [[n1403]]. Treat security software as a war hedge, not generic growth.
Narrative

Communication services is where sanctions policy meets platform economics. XLC closed at 68.53 USD, down 2.52% over 20 sessions, and Meta Platforms (FB) at 210.48 USD, down 28.56% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Reuters reported Meta barring Russian state media from running ads [[n0753]] and Google blocking RT and other Russian channels from earning ad dollars [[n0815]]: compliance now has a revenue cost.
Reported

Roblox suffered its worst post-earnings drop, per Bloomberg [[n0969]]; Nexstar reported fourth-quarter net revenue of $1.25 billion [[n1010]]; and The Hollywood Reporter's studio profit report had Disney diving while Sony soared [[n1061]].
EPS Upside Watch

Meta's Reels push is the swing factor for FB. Reuters reported the global launch of its 'fastest growing' format [[n0998]], and Ad Age reported new creator ad features aimed at TikTok [[n1009]]. Upside requires Reels monetisation to close the gap with feed advertising before engagement shifts further.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Content moderation has become a geopolitical liability as well as a brand risk. Reuters' focus on Spotify's Joe Rogan saga spotlighted podcast moderation challenges [[n1850]]; SPOT closed at 151.91 USD, down 11.33% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).

earnings_pattern.title: Guidance and cost discipline beat headline beats
parts: Rewarded

Block (SQ) was the clearest reward: the stock rose 26.14% to 119.82 USD on Friday and 15.19% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), after Payments Dive reported management defending higher marketing spending [[n1073]] and ABC reported Block soaring on the ASX as well [[n0061]]. Punished

Opendoor fell 23.13% after results that Barron's argued left the real-estate firm 'misunderstood' [[n0126]], and Dell fell 7.84% after missing its earnings goal [[n0714]]. CNBC reported Coinbase posting a big revenue beat but expecting first-quarter trading volume to fall [[n0554]]; COIN lost 7.86% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Newsweek reported Moderna's $12 billion 2021 profit [[n0606]], yet the shares fell 3.14%, and The Guardian reported Rolls-Royce losing £1.5bn of share value after its chief executive said he would quit [[n0628]].
Pattern

The market is paying for forward evidence and punishing caution on volumes, margins or leadership. Block and Carvana were rewarded for strategic moves that extend their platforms; Coinbase and Home Depot were punished despite beats because the outlook implied slower volumes or, in Home Depot's case, the margin warning Reuters flagged [[n1002]], while Moderna slipped even after its profit. With the 2Y up 37 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25), a beat on trailing numbers is worth less than a credible path for the next four quarters, and long-duration stories need cash-flow proof sooner.
Attention into EPS

The next prints will be judged on three disclosures. Russia exposure comes first, as UniCredit's statement that its Russian arm is self-funded and well covered [[n0670]] and Societe Generale's assurance that Rosbank operates normally [[n0649]] show. Input-cost pass-through comes second, which Reuters reported Coles flagging [[n0028]]. Chip supply is third, with Reuters reporting Ford halting F-150 output in Kansas City [[n1080]].
Playbook

Own post-earnings winners only where the outlook, not the beat, drove the move; Block holding above its 105.64 USD late-January close is the template (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Fade beats that arrive with volume or margin warnings. What changes the call: if sanctions disclosures reveal larger losses at European banks, punishment will widen from single names to whole sectors and the reward for good guidance will shrink.

New / Most Important

The BBC reported millions in bitcoin pouring into Ukraine from donors [[n0948]], giving crypto a wartime utility story. The SWIFT measures, which CNA explained as a possible path to sanction Russia [[n1404]], raise the question of whether sanctioned entities will try crypto rails, a risk that would invite tighter enforcement rather than adoption. Bloomberg also reported one of the biggest crypto traders tapping DeFi loans for funding [[n0934]], a reminder that leverage in the system is migrating, not disappearing.
Playbook

Action: size crypto as a high-beta risk asset, not a hedge, and keep it small while the VIX sits at 27.59 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Trigger to add: a daily close back above 43,840.29 USD, bitcoin's level of 2022-02-07 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-27), would show it decoupling from equity risk. What changes the call: evidence that sanctions enforcement targets exchanges, or regulatory movement on the spot ETF Peirce described; the former is a sell signal, the latter a durable bid.

flows.title: Liquidity is tightening into a war shock
parts: Global Liquidity

The liquidity regime was turning before the invasion. TD Economics argued quantitative tightening will slow deposit growth and put modest upward pressure on yields [[n0113]], and Capital Economics said 'we need to talk about QT' [[n1147]]. The IIF reported emerging markets driving global debt to a record $303 trillion [[n1249]], which leaves the system sensitive to a dollar-funding squeeze. The war adds a second channel: barring some Russian banks from SWIFT, as The New York Times reported [[n1412]], removes counterparties from the plumbing and encourages intermediaries to hoard liquidity. Primary markets are the first casualty: Riviera reported deteriorating conditions forcing Fred Olsen Windcarrier to put its IPO on hold [[n1237]], and the Luxembourg Times reported VW keeping the Porsche IPO on the table amid volatility [[n0788]]. When the issuance window shuts, sponsors waiting to exit stay locked in and fresh equity supply dries up, which supports index levels in the short run but starves the pipeline of growth listings.
Rates & Dollar

The dollar's haven move was brief. Reuters reported it jumping to a near two-year high on invasion day [[n1210]] before investors regained risk appetite and the dollar and oil pared gains [[n2160]]; the DXY closed Friday at 96.62 index points, up 0.86% over five sessions and down 0.66% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Treasuries left a positively sloped curve with the 2Y at 1.55% and the 10Y at 1.97%, bear-flattening over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25). Duration has paid nobody: TLT is down 4.34% and IEF 1.29% over 20 sessions, while SHY has lost only 0.60% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), so the front end remains the least costly place to hold liquidity. China Daily's argument that the yuan will remain an investor safe haven [[n0218]] is the policy-managed exception. The emerging-market transmission is visible: EMB closed at 100.17 USD, down 4.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), Reuters reported Indian shares and the rupee plunging as Russia attacked [[n1357]], and Forbes ranked the zloty among the biggest losers of the war's outbreak [[n1729]].
Credit Check

US credit is bending, not breaking. HYG closed at 83.61 USD, up 1.01% over five sessions and down 0.98% over 20, while LQD is down 3.20% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), a duration loss rather than a default signal. Stress is concentrated: Reuters reported Russian bonds hammered as the rouble plummeted [[n1332]], The Standard reported Fantasia being sued over its bond default [[n0170]], and Retail Banker International described Western sanctions slamming bank stocks [[n1975]]. China's property credit remains a slow-burn source of defaults, with CNBC reporting Moody's downgrading Shimao [[n0205]], and Brown Brothers Harriman is pitching structured credit as a toolbox against uncertain rate environments [[n1261]]. Issuers with access are locking in funding, as RBC Capital Markets' note on Ford's record $2.5 billion green bond shows [[n1250]].
Equity & Fund Flows

Flow evidence points to hard assets and defence. Reuters reported big inflows into gold ETFs on geopolitical concern [[n1255]], and the Financial Times reported ETF investors piling into Russian equities and defence stocks before the invasion [[n0904]], a bottom-fishing trade that the invasion-day crash in Russian stocks, which CNN put at 33% [[n0638]], promptly punished. Investopedia described investors fleeing stocks for refuge in gold and bonds [[n0675]]. Corporate buybacks remain the steadiest buyer: Time reported Buffett taking a 'mildly attractive' path with $27 billion of repurchases [[n0827]]. Among managers, Forbes reported Li Lu bulking up Meta and Bank of America while shedding Pinduoduo [[n0748]], Investor's Business Daily highlighted three shrewd moves by top Fidelity managers in a bad market [[n0780]], and CNBC asked readers who panic-sold during the week's volatility when to get back in [[n1969]], a measure of how fast sentiment swung.
Portfolio Implication

Price action overstates the all-clear. Friday's rally left the VIX at 27.59 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25) and a front end still repricing the Fed, and the weekend added SWIFT exclusions and German rearmament. Keep liquidity buffers higher than usual, prefer short-dated Treasuries to credit duration, hold gold and energy as the hedges that have worked, and treat the IPO and high-yield windows as shut until volatility settles. The signal to re-risk is two-sided: tighter HYG pricing and a weaker DXY together would show the funding channel easing, while a stronger dollar with falling EMB would show it seizing.

Conditional Expression

If the growth target and fiscal quota are ambitious, add to onshore exposure and to infrastructure-linked commodity names, with aluminium at 3,406.00 USD/t (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). If they are cautious, the onshore premium over offshore internet narrows and the relative trade should be cut.
Risk

Policy can ease while regulators keep tightening on platforms. Bloomberg's report of Alibaba planning for a new normal of low growth [[n0196]] says the offshore discount is about earnings power, not liquidity, so a stimulus package need not rescue KWEB. A Western move toward secondary sanctions would hit both legs.

catalysts.title: Block (SQ) — marketing spend rewarded
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Block rose 26.14% to 119.82 USD on Friday and 13.42% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), with Payments Dive reporting management defending higher marketing spending [[n1073]]. CNBC's account of Square's growth from scrappy hardware start-up to payments powerhouse [[n0584]] frames the thesis: spending to deepen the ecosystem is being rewarded while rates rise.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The hurdle is holding the gap above 105.64 USD, the late-January close (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The risk is that high-beta fintech re-rates lower as the 2Y climbs, which would close the gap regardless of execution.
Trade Expression
Buy pullbacks toward the gap rather than chasing; pair against PayPal, at 110.94 USD and down 29.83% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), to isolate execution from sector beta.

catalysts.title: Rheinmetall (RHM.DE) — Germany's rearmament proxy
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

DW reported Germany committing €100 billion to defence spending [[n1228]], and Reuters reported European defence stocks rising as Russia invaded [[n0565]]. Rheinmetall closed at 107.05 EUR, up 7.00% on Friday, 11.00% over five sessions and 15.06% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The question now is how quickly budget becomes orders.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock has already moved far above its 93.04 EUR late-January close (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Risk: procurement takes years, and a ceasefire would trigger profit-taking long before budgets are disbursed.
Trade Expression

Hold core exposure and add on pullbacks rather than chasing the gap; Joint Forces News' report of Rheinmetall presenting an HX 8×8 excavator with CSM [[n0768]] shows the HX truck platform's reach beyond combat orders.

catalysts.title: BP (BP.L) — the Rosneft exit
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

CNBC reported BP offloading its nearly 20% stake in Rosneft [[n0836]] after WSJ reported pressure from the UK government [[n0699]]. BP closed at 378.50 GBp, up 3.60% on Friday but down 1.80% over 20 sessions, while Shell is up 5.56% over 20 at 2,000.50 GBp (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The exit removes a sanctions overhang at the cost of whatever the stake contributed to earnings.
Price Hurdle & Risk
The first test is whether the market treats the decision as a write-down or as a de-risking. Risk: the size of the loss and the lost cash flow are not yet quantified.
Trade Expression

Prefer Shell over BP until BP quantifies the Rosneft hit, then reassess; a BP close above 385.45 GBp, its late-January level (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), would signal the market has looked through it.

catalysts.title: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK-B) — buybacks as the deal
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reported Buffett lamenting a lack of good investments even as Berkshire profit set a record [[n0807]], and Forbes Middle East put 2021 net profit at $89.8B [[n0837]]. BRK-B closed at 319.24 USD, up 3.56% on Friday and 3.76% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).

The risk is opportunity cost: without large acquisitions, returns rest heavily on buybacks. Business Insider reported Buffett blasting fake earnings [[n0826]], a reminder the stock is a cash-flow compounder, not a momentum vehicle.
Trade Expression
Own as quality ballast against long-duration growth; add if the price holds above 307.67 USD, its late-January close (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).

catalysts.title: Moderna (MRNA) — beat versus durability
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

WSJ reported Moderna beating profit estimates on COVID-19 vaccine sales [[n0602]], and CNBC reported the company expecting at least $19 billion in 2022 vaccine sales [[n0604]], while Fierce Pharma put its forecast at $22B [[n0605]]. BioPharma Dive reported Moderna advancing a 'bivalent' booster [[n0603]], but Fierce Biotech reported Merck cutting ties to its early KRAS vaccine [[n0601]]. Risk: pipeline setbacks matter more than booster volume once pandemic demand fades.
Trade Expression

Stay neutral; a close above 148.62 USD, the late-January level (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), keeps the range intact, while a break below it would signal the market is discounting the post-pandemic revenue cliff.

parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Modern Retail reported Alibaba betting on international growth as regulatory pressure grows [[n0534]], a sign that growth at home is harder to find. The US ADR closed at 107.94 USD, down 13.25% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
Price Hurdle & Risk

The hurdle is reclaiming 111.79 USD, the late-January close (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Risk to the bearish view: an aggressive stimulus package would lift all China assets, and The Japan Times' report of banks being told to report exposure to Ant [[n0161]] could also end in a resolution that removes an overhang.
